name: Dusty Red
lede: Dusty Red is a muted brick red that comes from the 2010 xkcd color-naming survey, where it was simply "dusty" put in front of [[red]].

sections.title: A survey name, not a dye
sections.body:
Our color library traces Dusty Red to the xkcd color survey of 2010, Randall Munroe's crowd-sourced exercise in which tens of thousands of volunteers typed free-text names for randomly shown colors, later cleaned into a standard list [1]. "Dusty" works the same way across that list, a grammar move that greys a base hue rather than a dye, place, or person behind the name [1].

The nearest named color in our graph is [[english-red]], at a color distance (ΔE2000) of 3.2, a slightly duller shade; its own near-twin [[dusty-crimson]] sits 4.0 away and reads duller still, while [[brick-red]] at 3.9 is more vivid [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds this brick red in 71 of 23,781 paintings, about 0.3 percent, as photographed [3]. It is strongest in Indian and Nepali painting, where the rate runs more than fifteen times the archive average, and in Kalighat work specifically, where it reaches nearly one painting in six [3]. These are photographs of aged, varnished paintings, so the figures are a computed color match, not a pigment test [3].
